title: The second reader, for the subsystems it covers -- 31 of 38 durable actions
note: R42 and R53 said the same thing from two directions: only authority records and tasks had an independent reconstruction, so the scheduler, policy, capability, agent, memory, network, secret and context projections were compared against a fresh replay of THEMSELVES -- which shares their reducer and therefore cannot see a shared misunderstanding. Every mutation here either makes the second reader agree with a forged history (so the differential check agrees with the attacker) or blinds it to a subsystem entirely (so it agrees by covering nothing, which is the quieter failure). R18-R24 attack the ownership and attempt-accounting rules. Before they existed the reader checked only the SHAPE of a transition -- job exists, src matches, not a revival -- and applied the payload verbatim, so it accepted a strictly wider language than the production reducer. That is the worst place for the gap to be: a log the primary refuses cannot be loaded, the two readers are never compared, and the permissive one is the only reader left. R29-R40 attack the escalation rules. Until they existed this reader had no escalation reconstruction at all, while the campaign was described as covering the second reader for EVERY subsystem -- two statements that could not both be true. R41-R74 attack the rules restated for P0-R12 (D-2026-27). Until then the authority and task replays at the top of reconstruct.py imported authority.check and tasks.check and handed every replayed record back to them -- so a weakened production gate was reproduced faithfully by the reader whose entire purpose is to disagree with it, and the differential comparison came back empty. These mutations come in three kinds: disable one restated rule (the reader accepts what production refuses), drift one restated table away from production (the conformance tests must name the difference), and re-couple the reader to the gate by import or by call (the AST guards must notice, including when the import hides in a function body). R75-R84 attack the two readers P0-R14 added (D-2026-29). agent.claim and task.compensation were the only uncovered actions a forged record of which changes what the system permits or whom it attributes a decision to: claims are the input to conflict resolution, and a compensation names the PERSON who authorized destroying something. The remaining seven are classified as not authority-changing in docs/identity_inventory.json, each with its reason, and the inventory now refuses a classification of authority-changing that has no second reader. R90-R97 attack the checkpoint-anchor reader added for D-2026-30. checkpoint.state is authority-changing -- it is what authorizes restoring a projection from a snapshot instead of replaying the log -- so R14's rule requires a second reader for it. R94 is the one to read: it does not remove a check, it makes the reader REPORT that it verified a head hash it never looked at. R98-R100 attack the same rule restated in the second reader (D-2026-31): what is canonical has to be the same question in both, or an empty diff means the two readers agreed about a verdict neither should have reached.
